questions.verification_notes: NHGRI Gene glossary, checked September 8, 2026, gives roughly 20,000 protein-coding genes and distinguishes genes that produce functional RNA. Corrects the scaled unit: the stored answer is now 20,000 genes, not 20 thousands.

expected.question_text: Approximately how many thousands of protein-coding genes are in the human genome?
expected.answer_context: Protein-coding genes are instructions used to make proteins. They are one part of the genome; counting genes does not count every protein the body can produce.

questions.question_text: Approximately how many genes in the human genome code for proteins?
questions.measure_definition: Approximate number of protein-coding genes, expressed as an ordinary count of genes. Excludes genes whose functional product is RNA rather than a protein.
questions.answer_context: About 20,000 genes contain instructions for making proteins. Other genes produce functional RNA instead, so this is not a count of every gene in the human genome.
